key_insight: Extending characteristic mapping to dissipative equations preserves its fine-scale resolution strategy while enabling applications such as Navier–Stokes flow.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a promising numerical route for resolving multiscale fluid dynamics across Reynolds-number regimes.
method: Lift scalar evolution equations to paths in a diffeomorphism group, interpreted through optimal transport.
Represent flow maps as compositions of spatial interpolants using semi-Lagrangian characteristic mapping.
Advance map components with semidirect-product evolution and integrate the log-Jacobian explicitly using an exponential integrator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-order accuracy and tests on canonical nonlinear dissipative equations, but provides no quantitative errors or computational benchmarks.
watch_item: Broad Reynolds-number applicability remains promising rather than established by the evaluation details given in the abstract.
paper_title: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations
